Definition
In this lesson, you will learn about the circuit loading effects of multimeters.timeters.
INTRODUCTIONM
All test equipment affects the circuit that is being measured.
Most test equipment is designed so the effect on the circuit is very small. very small.
For example, a digital multimeter's effect on a circuit is so small that normally it can not be measured. measured.
However, an analog multimeter has a noticeable effect on the circuit when measuring low voltages. oltages.
Knowing the loading effect of an analog multimeter is important when making circuit measurements. measurements.

Errors caused by the multimeter can lead you to incorrect conclusions on circuit operation.n circuit operation.
Ideally, a multimeter will not affect the circuit under
Realistically, multimeters affect the circuit under measurement because they have an internal resistance.al resistance.
The internal resistance (Rm) is either in series or in parallel to the circuit being measured.g measured.

To accurately measure circuit values, the internal resistance must be eliminated by multimeter design. r design.
If elimination is not possible, the effect of multimeter loading must be taken into consideration when measuring circuit values.
